xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-2858: Support Agent Client Protocol (ACP) harness — port t3code's effect-acp layer; first agent: Kimi Code CLI

plan.title: Support Agent Client Protocol (ACP) harness — port t3code's effect-acp layer; first agent: Kimi Code CLI
plan.author: agent:claude-fable-5

narratives.Problem: Overdeck has no way to run ACP-speaking agent CLIs (Kimi Code, Cursor, Grok, Gemini). Each new harness today costs a bespoke runtime adapter. ACP is a standard JSON-RPC-over-stdio protocol; one client implementation unlocks every ACP CLI, the same leverage codex app-server (PAN-2597) gave the GPT family. Kimi Code CLI (`kimi acp`) is the first target and positions us for Kimi K3 on Kimi's own agent loop.
narratives.Proposal: Vendor t3code's self-contained `packages/effect-acp` (Effect implementation of ACP; depends only on `effect`, verified compatible with our 4.0.0-beta.73) as a Bun workspace package with MIT attribution and upstream layout preserved for cheap future diffs. Port t3code's AcpRuntimeModel + AcpSessionRuntime into src/lib/acp/ with two trivial shims. Build a persistent per-agent ACP host process (tsdown entry `acp-host`, modeled on codex-app-server-host) that spawns the agent CLI, renders updates to the tmux pane, writes a transcript JSONL, and exposes a per-agent unix socket + token. Register a generic `acp` harness through the contracts behavior matrix and every validator site; wire launcher/spawn, a delivery tier in deliverAgentMessage, harness policy/resolve, config, transcript discovery, and frontend feed rendering. Kimi support module spawns `kimi acp` with an auth preflight. Docs + an opt-in real-binary probe test close it out.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No interactive permission prompting (AUQ integration); v1 implements acp.permissionMode 'auto' only — follow-up issue
- No cost/token-usage parsing for ACP sessions; adapter reports none — follow-up issue
- No Cursor/Grok/Gemini support modules; Kimi only in this issue
- No Effect upgrade to 4.0.0-beta.78; no repo-wide dependency churn
- No change to the kimi provider's built-in defaultHarness (stays claude-code; ACP is opt-in via providerHarnesses.kimi)
- No Docker-workspace ACP wiring (same exclusion as the PTY supervisor)
- No fs/* or terminal/* client capabilities advertised to the agent in v1 (capabilities stay off, matching upstream defaults)

autoDecisions.summary: Vendor effect-acp as Bun workspace package packages/effect-acp, not src/lib/acp/vendor/
autoDecisions.rationale: Preserves upstream import specifiers (effect-acp/client) and file layout 1:1 for cheap future diffs — the issue's stated goal — and escapes the src/-only file-size ratchet (schema.gen.ts is 10,375 lines vs the 1000-line ceiling). The issue offered either location; this one is strictly less invasive.

autoDecisions.summary: Generic 'acp' harness value with per-provider support modules; not a 'kimi-code' harness
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue names this as the preferred option ('acp with a per-provider spawn command'); one client for every ACP CLI is the entire leverage, and t3code's ~100-line Cursor/Grok modules prove the per-agent surface is tiny.

autoDecisions.summary: Persistent transport = per-agent host process (node dist/acp-host.js) mirroring codex app-server-host, with delivery-by-socket from day one
autoDecisions.rationale: Codex (PAN-2597) is the proven in-repo template: tmux-visible host, sockets/<kind>-<id>.sock + 0600 token, satisfies the no-one-shot-agents invariant; ACP sessions resume via session/load. Avoids codex's legacy dual one-shot/persistent split by making the socket path primary.

autoDecisions.summary: Effect stays at 4.0.0-beta.73; adapt beta.78 drift inside the vendored package, documented in VENDORING.md
autoDecisions.rationale: Verified all required unstable APIs (effect/Stdio, unstable/process/ChildProcess*, unstable/rpc/*) exist in beta.73; a repo-wide Effect bump for one feature is disproportionate risk to the dashboard.

autoDecisions.summary: Kimi ACP routing is opt-in (providerHarnesses.kimi: acp); built-in kimi defaultHarness stays claude-code
autoDecisions.rationale: The operator deliberately routes kimi via claude-code + coding endpoint today; harness routing is config-owned and defaults must not silently reroute live agents.

autoDecisions.summary: Permissions v1 = acp.permissionMode 'auto' only: pick the most permissive allow option from params.options at runtime; decline + log when none exists
autoDecisions.rationale: Matches t3code's outcome-mapping semantics while acknowledging optionIds are agent-specific (Cursor's allow-always/allow-once/reject-once are not universal); interactive prompting needs AUQ pipeline work that is separable and non-blocking for pipeline agents.

autoDecisions.summary: Kimi support module starts from Cursor's shape (no runtime wrapper), spawn = kimi acp
autoDecisions.rationale: Grok's shape exists only because xAI signals prompt completion out-of-band; Cursor's is the standard-conformant baseline. Kimi docs specify `kimi acp` as the ACP entry point.

autoDecisions.summary: Vendored tests keep upstream colocated src/*.test.ts layout; vitest include gains packages/effect-acp/src/**/*.test.ts
autoDecisions.rationale: Moving tests would break the 1:1 upstream mapping; a one-line include-glob addition is the smaller change.

narrative.Action: Create src/lib/acp/host.ts modeled closely on src/lib/codex/app-server-host.ts (read it first — it is the contract): a long-lived Node process the tmux session runs. main() parses --agent <id> --provider <name> --workspace <dir> [--resume <sessionId>] [--model <id>]. It resolves the provider's ACP support module (v1: kimi from src/lib/acp/kimi.ts via a small registry), builds the AcpSessionRuntime with the spawn input, registers handleSessionUpdate and handleRequestPermission BEFORE start() (effect-acp buffers notifications until a handler exists — ordering is load-bearing), then start()s. Delivery surface: bind unix socket ${OVERDECK_HOME}/sockets/acp-<id>.sock, write a bearer token file ${OVERDECK_HOME}/agents/<id>/acp-token at mode 0600, accept authenticated POST {op:'message', content} → forward to session/prompt (queue if a prompt is active — prompts are semaphore-serialized in the runtime), POST {op:'interrupt'} → cancel(). Mirror app-server-host's token verification header and socket cleanup on exit. Rendering: src/lib/acp/host-render.ts turns the parsed event stream into readable pane output (assistant text deltas, tool-call lines, plan updates) written to stdout — operator-visible via tmux. Transcript: src/lib/acp/transcript.ts appends ndjson entries (role, content, toolCalls, sessionId, timestamps) to ${OVERDECK_HOME}/agents/<id>/acp-session.jsonl including delivered orchestrator messages (transcript echo). Persist the ACP sessionId to ${OVERDECK_HOME}/agents/<id>/acp-session-id for resume. Auth preflight: if authenticate fails with auth-required, print the remediation ('run `kimi` in a terminal, then /login') to the pane and exit non-zero — never retry-loop. Add tsdown.config.ts entry 'acp-host': 'src/lib/acp/host.ts' beside the codex-app-server-host entry (line 17). All child-process and socket code is async-only (no execSync — server-reachable rule). Unit tests: socket rejects a wrong token with 401; accepted message reaches a stubbed runtime prompt and is echoed to the transcript; transcript JSONL lines parse.
